Analysis of network traffic # Number US 8,838,780 B2 HTML Dates 2009-02-02 — 2014-09-16 Inventors John Kane, Joseph Lawrence, Maria Farnon, Rick Nooner, Raoul Alcala, Mark Taylor Abstract Embodiments generally disclosed herein include a computer-implemented method for monitoring and correlating network traffic data associated with a primary network that is in communication with a plurality of secondary networks. The method generates a network traffic data set by monitoring network traffic between the primary network and the plurality of secondary networks. The method also determines a mapping of network connectivity by monitoring inter-network routing information between the primary network and the plurality of secondary networks. In addition, the method generates a traffic measurement data set by monitoring network utilization statistics between the primary network and the plurality of secondary networks. docs.text: Resume of John Arthur Kane PO Box 200, Firestone, CO 80520 Cell: (720) 204-2911 John.Kane@Kane.net Current Position # Senior Systems Administrator performing analytics work for GNI Operations — Edge Operations . I am primarily responsible for the Reporting needs of the Edge Operations team and make additional contributions for the larger GNI Operations . I am currently working towards a ladder change from the Systems Administrator Ladder to the Technical Program Manager Ladder . I have been with Google since July 2012. Before Google I worked at Level 3 Communications , a Tier 1 Network Provider, located in Broomeld, Colorado. While at Level 3 I served in various roles across Network Engineering , Information Technology and Content Distribution Networking . I have also worked at various other employeers prior to Level 3 , including Sprint Paranet (originally Paranet ), Texas A&M University , and Texas Instruments ); please see my Pre-Google Resume for more details of previous jobs. Accomplishments # Highlights # 5 1/2 year (started 2012-07-30) career at Google in the Edge Operations organization. I originally served as the TL/M for the EdgeOps team located in Thornton Colorado and have since evolved my role to be more analytics oriented. I developed a Headcount Model to allow GGC Ops to increase its headcount and justify a significant investment in automation development to forestall additional increases in headcount. I created a comprehensive set of reporting infrastructure and data ETL to support the needs of the GGC Ops / EdgeOps team. These dashboards have been used for various tactical and strategic efforts. I took a manual process that collected data from about a half-dozen different data sources and have automated that collection. This weekly report has been used for various traffic planning efforts of the NCD Team. Bringing in new talent to Google is essential for our growth. I previously was one of the most active interviewers in sistanizadeh@ organization with more than 100 interviews. I have received an SRE Interview Bonus and other recognitions from the recruiting teams. I organized a session of Statistical Thinking and More Statistical Thinking in BLD. These were the top rated courses in 2015 and recommended to our organization by sistanizadeh@. This effort allowed more than 175 Googlers in BLD and THN to attend a very valuable course, something they would have otherwise been unlikely to do. Signicant Project Accomplishments at Google # Google Start Date : 2012-Jul-30 - Thanks to kspessard@ for forcing me into the process. EdgeOps Reporting # I have developed or specified the majority of the reporting capabilities that EdgeOps possesses. This has been the creation of at least three generations of reporting tools and dashboards, migrating to the appropriate platforms as other platforms have been deprecated. I have worked to improve our data sources, detect anomalies, and provide more accurate views of that data. The reporting that was available at the beginning of my investigations and efforts were simple queries using Actionable Business Intelligence (ABI) and cherry-picking information from Bandaid XT Streaming Overview. I lead the effort that produced GGC Metrics and the reports underneath that facade. The GGC Metrics page has evolved and is being replaced by EdgeOps Metrics. This view is going to be replaced by capabilities provided by the new #plx dashboards. Reporting tools within Google have been a rapidly changing arena and moving to new platforms has not necessarily been the most effective use of resources, so much attention has been placed on underlying data quality and the ability to perform ad hoc data investigations. I have assisted team mates with those investigations by tutoring in using #plx and now colab notebooks. Weekly NCD Dashboard # This dashboard collects data from 7 different data sources, extracting capacity and utilization data from those sources. The information in this report is utilized by multiple departments as part of their decision making processes, including where to spend money by expanding our bandaid fleet footprint, our off-net network interconnections and traffic growth metrics. This report existed for more than six years as a sheet prior to my taking on the project. It suffers from excessive aggregation, presenting global roll-ups when data needs to be available at more granular levels, down to specific racks. This excessive aggregation has masked data issues that would have been visible if more granular data were available. I have worked to evolve this report into a more appropriate presentation of the data and to make the data more accessible to other teams. I have unmasked data calculations that were based upon ancient assumptions that were no longer valid and have lead to understated traffic volumes. Some of the underlying data is now available to other teams programmatically, the remaining data needs to be validated and made available as well. Once this is accomplished, the presentation needs to change to an online dashboard. This process has been plagued with problematic data sources and is one of the motivators for the data modeling work that I have undertaken. Loveshack Reporting Pipeline # TODO: Need some detail here NCD Weekly ETL # TODO: Need some detail here Exploration of New Technologies: Graph Databases # I investigated the use a graph database, a technology that is new to our team, as a possible tool to enhance our operational efforts. This project was a proto-typing / technology research effort designed to test the feasibility of enhancing Loveshack meta data and a mechanism for more dynamic reporting and root cause analysis. Working with stryth@ and zaks@, I: Negotiated with and eliminated a vendor (Neo Technology) due to pricing Selected a temporary implementation tool (Apache Jena) to enable Graph Database Exploration Developed a Use Case for determining the value of using a Graph Database for Edge Operations Reporting and Analytics Prepared a quick survey of Graph Database options Implemented a pilot system in Neo4j Implemented a pilot system in Apache Jena. The project completed but we did not decide to proceed with a full implementation due to demands on resources for workow automation development and planned data changes in Loveshack. This effort and lessons learned should be applicable for other projects in NetOps. Reporting Summit for EdgeOps # I organized two summits supporting Reporting and Analytics for Edge Operations (SYD 2015-June and ZUR 2015-December). These summits have allowed for improved communication between the members of EdgeOps, communications of priorities, sharing of tools and long-term planning. I have used these opportunities to multiply my efforts by recruiting additional engineering efforts from multiple regions, improving our capabilities. The establishment of a vision for reporting and analytics has improved our efforts by standardizing tools and approaches. Improving Data Quality Through Data Modeling # There has never been a cohesive approach to data within the NCD organization. We have many reports that purportedly tell the same story but their data are derived from different data repositories or present numbers that are calculated in different manners. The multitude of data sources is not documented, the interactions are not disclosed and deficiencies are not discussed. Issues with data collections, aggregations and reporting have occurred and they were not detected or properly communicated. This has led to reports being generated and decisions based on those reports. I have been documenting the data sources that are utilized in my reporting work, and have been attempting to track down the dependency chains. I have, where it has been possible, been implementing quality checks and measurements on that data. A lot of effort is needed to advance this problem, and I have been conducting an experiment with implementing a data model in a graph-based data store. I have most recently been using Neo4J due to its GUI and ease of use, but other graph databases may be the implementation target. I participated in two annual GraphConnect conferences hosted by Neo4J. During those conferences I have observed what other organizations have done in this area and have participated in training sessions on graphical databases and implementations. I have also had conversations with specialists from Neo4J and other companies about the problem domain that I care about (inventory, data modeling, etc) and possible approaches to these problems. While our problems are not unique, our scale, interdependencies and change velocity have provided lots of talking points. I continue to investigate solutions in this area. NCD must develop a comprehensive data model and a data / ETL inventory to reduce errors and provide richer and more accurate data for our decision processes. Team Documentation Modernization # Migration of team documentation to g3doc. I collaborated with bcable@ and greyburn@ to develop a framework and guidelines to migrate the team’s documentation from sites to g3doc. This project allows EdgeOps to modernize its documentation and provided a multi-regional mechanism for document review and approvals. I then extended that effort to the NCD Team site with the same goals in mind. This effort was grungy and not highly visible but was a solid contribution to improving EdgeOps eciency by reducing 5 - 7 years of dated materials to more effective documentation. Headcount Model for GGC Operations # I developed a Headcount Model to assist GGC Ops in justifying the growth in headcount needed by that organization to handle to exponential support costs. This model factored in the numbers of servers installed in the bandaid-xt eet as well as the number of interactions between the GGC Ops team and our partner ISPs. The model codied assumptions of automation impacts on eciencies. This allowed the team to grow during a explosive period of increasing support costs and to justify the signicant investment in automation development to forestall increases in stang. Signicant Non-Project Accomplishments at Google # Being Googley by Interviewing # Bringing in new talent to Google is essential for our growth. I have been one of the most active interviewers in sistanizadeh@’s organization, with 103 total interviews and a median latency to submit feedback of 0.21 days. I received an SRE Interview Bonus for that contribution. docs.text: This dashboard collects data from 7 different data sources, extracting capacity and utilization data from those sources. The information in this report is utilized by multiple departments as part of their decision making processes, including where to spend money by expanding our bandaid fleet footprint, our off-net network interconnections and traffic growth metrics. This report existed for more than six years as a sheet prior to my taking on the project. It suffers from excessive aggregation, presenting global roll-ups when data needs to be available at more granular levels, down to specific racks. I have worked to evolve this report into a more appropriate presentation of the data and to make the data more accessible to other teams. I have unmasked data calculations that were based upon ancient assumptions that were no longer valid and have lead to understated traffic volumes. Some of the underlying data is now available to other teams programmatically, the remaining data needs to be validated and made available as well. Once this is accomplished, the presentation needs to change to an online dashboard. This process has been plagued with problematic data sources and is one of the motivators for the data modeling work that I have undertaken.

docs.text: There has never been a cohesive approach to data within the NCD organization. We have many reports that purportedly tell the same story but their data are derived from different data repositories or present numbers that are calculated in different manners. The multitude of data sources is not documented, the interactions are not disclosed and deficiencies are not discussed. Issues with data collections, aggregations and reporting have occurred and they were not detected or properly communicated. This has led to reports being generated and decisions based on those reports. I have been documenting the data sources that are utilized in my reporting work, and have been attempting to track down the dependency chains. I have, where it has been possible, been implementing quality checks and measurements on that data. A lot of effort is needed to advance this problem, and I have been conducting an experiment with implementing a data model in a graph-based data store. I have most recently been using Neo4J due to its GUI and ease of use, but other graph databases may be the implementation target. I participated in two annual GraphConnect conferences hosted by Neo4J. During those conferences I have observed what other organizations have done in this area and have participated in training sessions on graphical databases and implementations. I have also had conversations with specialists from Neo4J and other companies about the problem domain that I care about (inventory, data modeling, etc) and possible approaches to these problems. While our problems are not unique, our scale, interdependencies and change velocity have provided lots of talking points. I continue to investigate solutions in this area. NCD must develop a comprehensive data model and a data / ETL inventory to reduce errors and provide richer and more accurate data for our decision processes.
